# Business English — Syria — unit map

CEFR band: **B1 to B2**. Units: **12**. Pages: **84**. Scenes: **571**. Scored items: **1272**.

**This file is generated.** Run `node tools/unitmap.js` from `business-sy/app`.

Each unit runs over the same seven pages, and the item budget on each page is
fixed by `assets/book.js`, not chosen per unit. The task names in the last
column are the Cambridge Business English task types recorded in
`assets/spec.js`, except `sentence-build`, `pronounce-pair` and `review`,
which that file marks as this course's own.

## The seven pages

| Code | Page | Kind | Published task budget per unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `l1` | Vocabulary | lesson | read-cloze ×12, read-notices ×4 |
| `l2` | Writing | lesson | write-internal ×2, write-correspondence ×2, sentence-build ×6 |
| `l3` | Grammar | lesson | sentence-build ×10, read-proofread ×6 |
| `l4` | Meetings & Calls | lesson | listen-extracts ×12, listen-note-conversation ×8, pronounce-pair ×8 |
| `l5` | Reading at Work | lesson | read-match-text ×4, read-article ×6, read-graphic ×6 |
| `oc` | At Work | work | listen-note-monologue ×6, listen-discussion ×8 |
| `tw` | Teamwork & Language Review | review | write-correspondence ×2, speak-interview ×4, review ×12 |

## Unit 1 — Introducing the Business

**Field:** SME company profile

**Grammar:** present and past verb forms; yes/no questions and answers; adjectives and adverbs  
**Word building:** dis- and re-  
**Pronunciation:** sh, ch and j  
**Chart:** line  
**At Work:** show that you are following a briefing

**Writing strategy:** one idea to a paragraph in a company description  
**Reading strategy:** reading with a purpose; reading a trend line more than once

| Page | Objective | Scenes | Items | Published tasks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `l1` | Describe what a company makes, where it sells and how it is organised | 8 | 16 | read-cloze ×12, read-notices ×4 |
| `l2` | Write a short internal message and a first reply to an enquiry | 7 | 10 | sentence-build ×6 *, write-correspondence ×2, write-internal ×2 |
| `l3` | Use present and past forms to say what a company does and what it did | 7 | 16 | read-proofread ×6, sentence-build ×10 * |
| `l4` | Answer a short work question, and take notes from a call | 6 | 28 | listen-extracts ×12, listen-note-conversation ×8, pronounce-pair ×8 * |
| `l5` | Read a company profile and a sales chart, and find the line that answers a question | 7 | 16 | read-article ×6, read-graphic ×6, read-match-text ×4 |
| `oc` | Follow a briefing and show the speaker you are following it | 5 | 14 | listen-discussion ×8, listen-note-monologue ×6 |
| `tw` | Write the two emails this unit has been building towards, and answer questions about your own work | 8 | 6 | speak-interview ×4, write-correspondence ×2 |

## Unit 2 — Plans, Quotes and Promises

**Field:** quotation and order confirmation

**Grammar:** be going to and will; plans, promises and predictions; would rather + verb  
**Word building:** -ful and -less  
**Pronunciation:** j and ch  
**Chart:** pie  
**At Work:** disagree politely in a planning meeting

**Writing strategy:** writing a quotation that commits to a date  
**Reading strategy:** understanding the labels on a revenue split

| Page | Objective | Scenes | Items | Published tasks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `l1` | Use the words a quotation is made of, and say what each one commits you to | 8 | 16 | read-cloze ×12, read-notices ×4 |
| `l2` | Write a quotation that commits to a date, and an internal note that does not | 7 | 10 | sentence-build ×6 *, write-correspondence ×2, write-internal ×2 |
| `l3` | Choose between will and going to, and say what you would rather do | 7 | 16 | read-proofread ×6, sentence-build ×10 * |
| `l4` | Answer questions about price and date, and take notes from a negotiation call | 6 | 28 | listen-extracts ×12, listen-note-conversation ×8, pronounce-pair ×8 * |
| `l5` | Read terms of sale and a revenue split, and find the line that commits you | 7 | 16 | read-article ×6, read-graphic ×6, read-match-text ×4 |
| `oc` | Disagree with a plan without damaging the person who made it | 5 | 14 | listen-discussion ×8, listen-note-monologue ×6 |
| `tw` | Announce a price increase, hold a price under pressure, and answer for both | 8 | 6 | speak-interview ×4, write-correspondence ×2 |

---

`*` marks a task type this course invented rather than one Cambridge
publishes. `assets/spec.js` is the single place that distinction is recorded,
and `tools/check.js` reads it, so a scene cannot quietly claim an authority
the handbook does not give it.
